To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the offline evaluation of the click prediction model is highly misleading and (2) the online evaluation paradigm we designed can be used to evaluate the predictive model performance in the future.

the discrepancy between offline and online metrics for predictive models can be substantial, that the discrepancy is due to the fact that the model is evaluated on a fixed set of ads, and that the discrepancy can be reduced by simulating the online behavior of the model.
the offline metrics are not reliable indicators of model performance in online environments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the characteristics and behaviors the offline evaluation metrics and the discrepancy between the offline performance and online behavior of predictive model.
the accuracy of evaluation methods for predictive models and the discrepancy between the offline model performance and the real online model performance.
a fundamental problem in predictive analytics: the discrepancy between offline and online evaluation metrics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
offline evaluation is a necessary but not sufficient condition for a good online predictive model.
the discrepancy between offline and online performance depends on the nature of the predictive model.
offline metrics should be used with caution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have designed a new evaluation paradigm for predictive models that is more consistent with their online performance and we have identified some of the characteristics of offline evaluation metrics that could lead to significant discrepancy between the offline performance and online performance of predictive models.
the online performance of a prediction model can be estimated with reasonable accuracy if we have a good understanding of the user behavior in the online environment.
we have developed a new paradigm that simulates online user behavior for model evaluation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the online behavior of a model is a better indicator of the actual model performance on real user data.
the discrepancy between offline and online metrics is a result of the characteristics of the predictive models and the online testing environment.
offline evaluation metrics should be interpreted with care, and we should design new metrics that better reflect the online model behavior.
